## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `--json` takes the next argument as its path even when that argument is another flag, so the default-destination form breaks whenever `--json` comes before `--junit`. This review traced `parse_args` and `write_reports` in `app/cli.py` against the inputs the PR describes, and read the two tests in `tests/test_cli.py` without running them. The new `--junit` check at `app/cli.py:7` rejects both a missing path and a following flag, and `test_required_junit_path` tests both cases.

## Changes
The PR adds a `--json` option to `parse_args`. With no path it writes to `results.json`; with a path it writes there. It also adds `write_reports`, which writes each parsed report to its destination, and a new `tests/test_cli.py` that covers the default `--json` path, an explicit `--json` path and the `--junit` path checks.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Stop `--json` from consuming a following flag as its path — With `["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"]`, `parse_args` sets `options["json"] = "--junit"`, skips past it, and then raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. Lines 15–19 check only `i + 1 < len(args)`, so any next argument becomes the path. `--junit` at line 7 also rejects arguments that start with `--`, but this branch does not. With `["--json", "--junit"]`, `write_reports` writes the JSON report to a file named `--junit`. That also makes the comment at line 12 ("JSON can use its default destination when no path is supplied") false for this input. — The PR body says `--json` can use its default "alongside the required --junit destination". Users who put `--json` first get either a misleading unknown-option error or a stray file, instead of `results.json` plus their JUnit report. — Fix: Take `args[i + 1]` as the destination only when it exists and does not start with `--`, matching line 7. Then add a test such as `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]) == {"json": "results.json", "junit": "x.xml"}`.
